name: Media-TIC
features: Steel-framed cube wrapped in inflatable ETFE cushions that shade the offices from the sun.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2011
note: No English Wikipedia article; year 2010 is from memory (it won WAF 2011). Fourth photo is a close-up of the ETFE cushions.

name: LocHal
by: Civic Architects, Braaksma & Roos, Inside Outside (Petra Blaisse)
features: 1932 locomotive shed turned public library; huge movable textile screens divide the vast hall.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2019

photos.file: File:Exterieur aanzicht Bibliotheek LocHal Tilburg, april 2019.jpg

note: Officially opened January 2019 (some sources say 2018). Mecanoo designed the library interior. Second photo has a construction fence in front.

name: Dornbusch Church
features: 1960s church partly torn down and closed by a new wall keeping imprints of the old; its footprint is marked outside.
award: World Architecture Festival 2008: Religion category winner
note: Firm's site gives completion 2005 (Wikipedia: 2004-2006). The traced outline is visible as lines in the paving in the second photo; check wording if unsure.

name: Unilever-Haus
features: Offices around a tall open atrium, wrapped in a loose ETFE foil skin against the harbour wind.
award: World Architecture Festival 2009: Office category winner
note: Facts from memory (Behnisch, HafenCity, 2009, ETFE outer skin, central atrium open to the public at ground level). Second photo is a distant view from the Elbe with the Elbphilharmonie.

name: City of Justice
by: David Chipperfield Architects, b720 Fermín Vázquez Arquitectos
features: Courts in separate tall blocks of tinted concrete in different colours, linked by a shared low base.
award: World Architecture Festival 2010: Civic & Community category winner
commons_category: Category:Ciutat de la Justícia de Barcelona i l'Hospitalet de Llobregat
note: No English Wikipedia article. Commons has dozens more photos of each block (files 33-56 by one author, CC BY 4.0).

name: Quay Quarter Tower
features: A 1970s office tower kept and grown: its core reused, wrapped in five shifted, stacked glass boxes.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2022

photos.file: File:Sydney Quay Quarter Tower seen from Pitt Street.jpg

note: Upcycled AMP Centre (1976). Many 2023 photos in the category show it with Governor Phillip Tower.

name: Aviva Stadium
features: Bowl that drops low on one side to spare neighbours' light, wrapped in a rippling skin of clear louvres.
award: World Architecture Festival 2010: Sport category winner
note: Third photo is the glazed entrance close up.

name: Max Aicher Arena
features: Hall about 200 m by 90 m with no inner columns, roofing over the old outdoor speed-skating oval.
award: World Architecture Festival 2011: Sport category winner

photos.file: File:Inzell, de Max Aicher Arena foto7 2017-08-05 12.39.jpg

note: Covered 400 m speed-skating oval. Column-free span and rooflights from memory and the interior photo File:Evo2 Max-Aicher-Arena.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0), which shows the inside well. Pohl Architekten co-credit from memory; check.

name: Kurilpa Bridge
features: Tensegrity footbridge: masts and cables at scattered angles hold the deck and its small shade canopies.
award: World Architecture Festival 2011: Transport category winner

photos.file: File:AUS Brisbane, Central Business District, Kurilpa Bridge 002.jpg
File:Brisbane's Kurilpa Bridge, the day before it opened. (4044806684).jpg

note: Second photo is a black-and-white silhouette; third a close-up of masts and canopies.

name: Royal Children's Hospital
by: Billard Leece Partnership and Bates Smart
features: Curving ward blocks with coloured leaf-like fins look over Royal Park; a tall street-like atrium inside.
award: World Architecture Festival 2012: Health category winner

photos.file: File:The Royal Children's Hospital as seen from Royal Park Melbourne.jpg

note: Second photo is a high view from the park. File:Royal-Childrens-Hospital-Melbourne.JPG seems to show older buildings, so skip it. Interior: File:Royal Children's Hospital Atrium Melbourne.jpg (CC BY 2.0).

name: Victoria Tower
features: Slim hotel tower clad in faceted glass triangles that scatter the sky, with a notch cut near the top.
award: World Architecture Festival 2012: Hotel & Leisure category winner
note: Second photo is a facade close-up. File:Victoria Tower Kista 2.jpg shows it under construction. Wikipedia: 117 m, 34 floors, completed 2011.

name: Maersk Tower
features: Research tower on a low landscaped base, wrapped in copper shutters that move with the sun.
award: World Architecture Festival 2017: Higher Education & Research category winner
note: University of Copenhagen Panum extension.

name: Daikanyama T-Site
features: Three low bookshop pavilions linked by a walkway, skinned in a lattice of interlocking white Ts.
award: World Architecture Festival 2012: Shopping category winner
note: Tsutaya Books. Type: no retail type in vocab, so Culture & sport; change if preferred. First photo is a dusk view of two pavilions; the T lattice reads better in the second.

name: Dialogue Centre Przełomy
features: History museum hidden under a city square whose paving rises into slopes; a hard-edged pavilion marks one corner.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2016
note: No dedicated Commons category found (files sit in Category:Museums in Szczecin and others). First photo is a drone view showing the whole square; second shows the pavilion. Branch of the National Museum in Szczecin.

name: Surat Diamond Bourse
features: Nine 15-storey office towers joined by a central spine, with landscaped courts between them.
award: World Architecture Festival 2023: Office category winner
note: Only aerial photos (drone views, the second straight down on the courts); no ground-level view on Commons. Often called the world's largest office building.

name: Qatar Faculty of Islamic Studies
features: Faculty and mosque raised on five big columns, one per pillar of Islam, with two 90 m calligraphic minarets.
award: World Architecture Festival 2015: Religion category winner
note: Only ~1125px photos, mostly of the minarets (pass the 800px rule). Qatar has no freedom of panorama, so these files could be deleted from Commons; a drawing would be a backup. Now part of Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Education City. Wikipedia (Education City Mosque) gives 90 m minarets and five columns, and says finished 2013, but a Commons photo shows it under construction in 2014, so 2015 is kept.

name: Arena Zagreb
features: Oval arena wrapped in 86 curved white concrete ribs that hold up a cable-hung roof spanning 110 m.
award: World Architecture Festival: Structural Design (Spans) award
note: WAF lists it under the Structural Design (Spans) awards; check the year on the WAF page. Third photo shows only one end under a storm sky.

name: Museum of Memory and Tolerance
features: Seven-level concrete and steel museum facing the Alameda, wrapped round an atrium with a floating Children's Memorial.
award: World Architecture Festival: Culture category winner
note: Photos are 1200px, donated by the museum. Architect and year from memory (Arditti + RDT, opened 2010); WAF page lists it as a Culture winner without the year clearly shown, check.

name: U.S. Bank Stadium
features: Sharp prow and steep clear ETFE roof that sheds snow; a glass wall with giant pivoting doors.
award: World Architecture Festival 2017: Sport category winner
note: Second photo is a drone view showing the roof and the plaza.

name: TKTS Booth, Father Duffy Square
by: Choi Ropiha, Perkins Eastman, PKSB Architects
features: Ticket booth under a flight of glowing red glass steps that doubles as seating over Times Square.
award: World Architecture Festival 2009: New & Old category winner

photos.file: File:TKTS - Times Square, New York, NY, USA - August 19, 2015 01.jpg

note: Competition concept by Choi Ropiha (Sydney), 1999; structural glass stair. Type could also be Pavilion.

name: Scale Lane Bridge
features: Swing footbridge that people can stay on while it pivots to let boats pass; its drum sits on the bank.
award: World Architecture Festival 2014: Transport category winner
commons_category: Category:Scale Lane Bridge, Kingston upon Hull

photos.file: File:Scale Lane Bridge Span Overview, Kingston upon Hull Feb25.jpg

note: The first photo shows the drum end from the plaza, the second the span from the river side.

name: Hotel Jakarta
features: Timber-framed hotel on the tip of Java Island, built around a glass-roofed subtropical garden.
award: World Architecture Festival 2018: Hotel & Leisure category winner
note: Commons category is named after the address. Interior garden: File:2023 Amsterdam, Hotel Jakarta (02).jpg. Timber structure from memory (timber above a concrete base); check.

name: Ravenscar House Museum
features: House museum of precast concrete faced with crushed earthquake rubble, its rooms set out like a home by a courtyard.
award: World Architecture Festival 2023: Culture category winner
note: Only one photo (4032x1737), a clear street view. Opened November 2021 (from memory).

name: University Children's Hospital Zurich
features: Low three-storey hospital laid out like a town of streets and courtyards; patient rooms are wooden cottages on top.
award: Dezeen Awards 2025: Architecture Project of the Year
view: Schematic long elevation: two timber-screened lower floors with the row of patient-room cottages, each with its own roof pitch, along the top floor.
note: No photos on Commons yet (Switzerland has freedom of panorama, so a new upload is likely). Sources: 114 top-floor rooms, each a wooden cottage with its own roof of varying slope; three storeys; courtyards. The drawing is schematic: cottage count, windows and facade rhythm are simplified, and the separate research and teaching building is left out. The Dezeen 2025 win comes from a secondary source (Aspire Metro).

name: Sony City Osaki (NBF Osaki Building)
features: Office slab whose long face is lined with porous ceramic louvre pipes that cool the air by evaporating rainwater.
award: World Architecture Festival 2012: Production, Energy & Recycling category winner
note: Only one photo (3648px), a low view of the louvred facade with the Sony sign still on top. Renamed NBF Osaki Building after Sony sold it. 'BioSkin' facade details from memory.

name: Belarusian Memorial Chapel
features: Small timber chapel modelled on Belarus's wooden churches, cedar-shingled, a memorial to the victims of Chernobyl.
award: World Architecture Festival 2018: Religion category winner

photos.file: File:Belarusian Memorial Chapel, North Finchley, July 2023.jpg
File:Church of St Cyril of Turau and All the Patron Saints of the Belarusian People (2016-11-24).jpg

note: Church of St Cyril of Turau, North Finchley; memorial to the victims of Chernobyl. Materials from memory and the photos; check 'oak'.

name: Central Saint Martins, Granary Building
features: An 1850s granary and its sheds turned into an art school, joined by a long top-lit internal street.
award: World Architecture Festival 2012: Higher Education & Research category winner

photos.file: File:University of the Arts, London - geograph.org.uk - 3378403.jpg

note: The award is for Stanton Williams' conversion and new building behind the 1852 granary (Lewis Cubitt). The photos show the historic front; the new internal street is File:Central St Martins Art School 0802.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0), worth adding.

name: Victoria Gate
features: Department store in a woven-looking terracotta diagrid that recalls Leeds textiles, beside glass-roofed arcades.
award: World Architecture Festival 2017: Shopping category winner

photos.file: File:Victoria Gate seen across St. Peter's Street, Leeds (13th December 2018).jpg

note: Shopping centre (no retail type in vocab, so Public space). Category has ~60 more photos, mostly 1280px geograph views of the development. Textile reference is from memory; check.

name: Quzhou Stadium
features: Stadium half-buried under grassy mounds shaped like nearby ridges, under a floating white membrane ring roof.
award: World Architecture Festival 2023: Sport category winner
view: Side elevation: grass-covered earth mounds in front, the thin halo-like PTFE canopy floating above on slender supports.
note: No photos on Commons. Sources: 30,000 seats, 250 m PTFE canopy described as a halo or floating cloud on nine pillars, earth-sheltered with sloped grassy facades echoing mountain ridges. The drawing is schematic: mound profile, canopy thickness and number of visible supports are not taken from a measured drawing. Wikipedia carries an unverified-text banner and gives opening as both 2021 and 2022; Dezeen reported completion in October 2022.

name: Holy Redeemer Church and Community Centre, Las Chumberas
features: Four massive concrete blocks like split rocks rise from a dug-out crater; picón stone in the chipped concrete.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2025
note: No photos on Commons (Spain has freedom of panorama, so an upload would be allowed). Not drawn: sources say four massive fractured concrete volumes on a steep slope, but I couldn't establish their individual shapes and heights from text. Completion year: designboom covered it as complete in March 2022; check. Long-running project (Menis started it in the 2000s).

name: Santa Maria Goretti Church
features: White concrete church on a four-leaf-clover plan of rising cylinders, lit from above through skylights.
award: World Architecture Festival 2023: Religion category winner
note: The Commons category exists but holds no files (Italy has no freedom of panorama). Not drawn: sources give the clover plan, white concrete cylinders with a flat roof and skylights, and a parish centre with a scalloped green roof, but not the relative heights of the lobes. A good drawing candidate if the owner finds a reference elevation.

name: Sara Kulturhus
features: Culture centre and 20-storey hotel tower built in timber; the hotel is stacked prefabricated CLT room modules.
award: World Architecture Festival 2022: Culture category winner
note: Second photo is at night with the tower lit in colours. Earlier files in the category show construction (useful as extras: exposed timber frame). Hotel is The Wood Hotel; storey count from memory, check.

name: Forskaren
features: Round seven-storey life-science hub, its glass facade lined with vertical wooden slats, around a large central atrium.
award: World Architecture Festival 2024: Office category winner
note: Files are named 'Kvarteret Forskaren, Hagastaden' (no own category found). Some April 2022 files show it under construction; 'Norra tornen och kvarteret Forskaren ... oktober 2022' files show it finished from further away. Atrium detail is from memory; check.

name: Paula Fox Melanoma and Cancer Centre
features: Six-storey cancer centre on St Kilda Road, wrapped in a light-filtering facade veil modelled on healthy skin.
award: World Architecture Festival 2024: Health category winner
note: Only one photo (3024px square, public domain), a clear street view. At Alfred Hospital, Prahran; year from memory (opened 2023), check.

name: Alila Villas Uluwatu
features: Clifftop resort of low terraced villas and open lattice pavilions, built with local stone and reclaimed timber.
award: World Architecture Festival 2010: Holiday category winner
note: Flickr photos with generic titles (Pavilion, Paradise, Dusk) but in the building's own category. Materials from memory (volcanic stone, reclaimed ironwood); check.

name: Shanghai Suhe MixC World
features: Shopping centre under a park on Suzhou Creek: planted slopes step down into an "urban valley" to the shops.
award: World Architecture Festival 2023: Shopping category winner
note: Only one photo (6559px): the sunken valley and green terraces, with a large pink elephant sculpture in the foreground. Opening year from memory (2021), check. No retail type in vocab, so Public space.

name: Simba Vision Montessori School
features: Two-storey school of volcanic-rock blockwork walls set at angles for airflow, under a deep overhanging zinc roof.
award: Dezeen Awards 2023: Architecture Project of the Year
note: No photos on Commons. Not drawn: sources describe angled blockwork walls and an overhanging zinc roof that collects rain, but not the overall plan shape or roof profile. Completion 2022 per one listing; Dezeen gives no year. Serves Maasai communities between Mount Meru and Kilimanjaro.

name: Blaise Pascal High School Gymnasium
features: Bare-concrete sports hall on a slope, its upper level wrapped in red perforated metal louvres for shade and breeze.
award: World Architecture Festival 2018: Sport category winner
note: No photos on Commons. Not drawn: sources give the concrete base, steel upper level with red perforated louvres, no air conditioning, and West Africa's first indoor climbing wall, but not the roof shape or proportions. Completion year is my estimate (shortlisted WAF 2018); check.

name: Darlington Public School
features: Angular brick school with a sawtooth roof; curved metal screens wrap open-air terraces; Aboriginal art in the cladding.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2024
note: No photos on Commons (Australia has freedom of panorama for buildings, so an upload would be allowed). Not drawn: sources give the sawtooth roof, brick and curved screens, but not storey count or how the screens sit on the elevation. Re-opened July 2023. fjcstudio (formerly FJMT) also won in 2013 with Auckland Art Gallery.

name: Huizhen High School
by: Approach Design Studio, Zhejiang University of Technology Engineering Design Group
features: Boarding school with elevated walkways and a ramp up to a gently sloping roof that is a park and open-air lecture hall.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2023
note: No photos on Commons. Not drawn: sources mention a rooftop park, treehouses, elevated walkways in a 'floating forest' and a sloping roof reached by a ramp, but not the massing. Completion year is my estimate from the 2023 award.

name: Guangming Village Post-earthquake Reconstruction
by: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Edward Ng, Mu Jun and team)
features: Prototype village house rebuilt after the 2014 Ludian earthquake in improved, earthquake-resistant rammed earth.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2017
note: No photos on Commons. Not drawn: I could not reach a description of the house's form. Team names, earthquake (Ludian, 2014) and completion year are from memory; check before use.

name: The Chapel
features: Low-budget community hall of leftover steel frame and sheet; printed fabric on the windows throws coloured light.
award: World Architecture Festival: World Building of the Year 2014
note: No photos on Commons. Not drawn: sources describe materials (reused steel frame and sheets, a tree-shaped steel column, three layers of printed fabric) but not the outer form. Year 2014 is the award year; completion may be 2013.

name: Dalarna Media Library
features: University library clad in larch behind horizontal polished-steel slats; a spiral ramp rises round its atrium.
award: World Architecture Festival 2014: Higher Education & Research category winner
note: Dalarna University's library in Falun, both photos in snow. The second file's embedded metadata says 'Todos os dereitos reservados' (all rights reserved) although Commons lists CC BY-SA 4.0 - check its file page before using it. Year and slat material from memory; check.

name: London Bridge Station
features: Rebuilt station with a huge street-level concourse under the tracks and long curved canopies over the platforms.
award: World Architecture Festival 2018: Transport category winner
note: Award is for the 2013-2018 rebuild. First photo shows the new platform canopies; second the Tooley Street entrance through the old arches with the Shard above; third is the concourse interior (inside, so maybe not the cover).

name: Lanserhof Sylt
features: Health resort under Europe's largest thatched roof; ridge and eaves swing with the dunes, loggias cut into the thatch.
award: World Architecture Festival 2023: Hotels & Leisure category winner
view: Schematic long elevation of the main building: low glazed ground floor under a deep overhanging thatched roof with a gently swinging ridge and eaves and loggias cut into the roof.
note: No photos on Commons (Germany has freedom of panorama, so an upload would be allowed). Sources: 7,100 m2 thatched roof on 1,348 glulam rafters, main building in three sections under one roof, overhanging thatch modelled on a 1930s officers' building, loggias set into the roof. The drawing is schematic: number of loggias, storey height and roof profile are not measured. Completion 2022 (earlier target 2020).
